thread:
jas: uploaded a pair of Figma frames for 'compact rail' + breadcrumb-first variant: https://figma.redwood/nav/compact-rail. Quick thoughts?

kevin: clean visually. My main concern: permalink shape. If we show only icons, will links still contain workspace/group path? important for analytics and external sharing.

samira: Yes keep the full path in the URL. UX should be compact visually but canonical URLs should be explicit: /org/:orgId/ws/:wsId/... makes intent clear in screenshots.

jas: thinking aloud: show icons, breadcrumb shows full labels, and router always resolves to canonical long path. short legacy paths should redirect.

lucas: ok but implementation detail: if we auto-redirect short -> long we should use history.replaceState so back button doesn't trap users on the intermediate short URL. otherwise it's confusing.

kevin: Agreed. Proposed router ordering (long first, then legacy short) so new canonical routes win. if legacy matched, call a resolver svc and replaceState to canonical. Pseudocode:
```
// routing layer
if (routeMatches('/org/:org/ws/:ws/model/:id')) render();
else if (routeMatches('/model/:id')) {
  const ws = resolveWsForModel(id);
  history.replaceState(null, '', `/org/${ws.org}/ws/${ws.id}/model/${id}`);
  render();
}
```

samira: Accessibility checklist: when rail collapses to icons we need: aria-label on each icon button, visible focus outline, skip-to-main link, and a way to expand via keyboard (a chevron toggle). Also ensure screen reader breadcrumb reads full path (not just icons).

jas: note: when opening a deep link in a new tab, we should probably render the expanded rail briefly or animate reveal so users get context, then allow them to collapse. Otherwise they land in a compact UI with no obvious context.

lucas: animation aside, that's a UX choice. But tests should assert that deep link landing state includes breadcrumb with humanized names and that the left rail has the active item highlighted even if collapsed.

kevin: Copy nit for breadcrumbs: prefer "Workspace: Payments › Model: pricing-v2" over slug-only. That reads better in emails/screenshots. Also use › as crumb separator for screen reader clarity.

samira: keyboard behaviour: tabbing into breadcrumb should focus the nearest actionable crumb (the right-most). If the crumb's parent group is collapsed, focusing it should programmatically expand that group (or open a mini-menu) so keyboard users can navigate.

jas: question: should collapsed icons show only native tooltips or an ARIA popup with label+shortcut? tooltips are fine for mouse but invisible to keyboard/screen reader. maybe tooltips + persistent visible label on first hover/focus for discoverability.

lucas: agree: provide aria-describedby pointing to an offscreen label and also a visible tooltip for pointer. keep a short animation to avoid layout shift.

design-bot: reminder: upload both collapsed/expanded Figma frames to /boards/nav-ia and tag @design for review. Usability test slot booked Fri 2pm. :spiral_calendar:

jas: I'll add a small layer in figma outlining router contract and the a11y checklist, plus a couple of edge-case flows (legacy short links, open-in-new-tab, and share-screenshot state). thanks all :thumbsup:
